description:
FILED s465bb (Opus, round 23, 2026-09-03) from the #994 probe battery.  PRE-EXISTING and identical on the base tree (1fed80b), on the branch, and under PCL_OPT=none â it is the coercion table, not an optimizer regime.

THE BUG.  A raw ARRAY value reaching STRING context stringifies as a REFERENCE.  perl gives the element COUNT (an array in scalar context is its count, and string context is scalar context); PCL gives `ARRAY(0x1)`.

  my @a = (7,8,9);
  print @a . "", "\n";            # perl 3      PCL ARRAY(0x1)
  sub f { @a } print f() . "";    # perl 3      PCL ARRAY(0x1)
  print lc(f());                  # perl 3      PCL array(0x1)
  print length(f());              # perl 1      PCL 10   (length of "ARRAY(0x1)")
  print +(f() eq '3') ? "EQ":"NE";# perl EQ     PCL NE

Probe: scratch/arrstr.pl and scratch/arrctx.pl in the s465bb worktree (both run under perl and ./runpcl side by side).

WHAT IS RIGHT ALREADY (measured, same probe): NUMERIC context (`f() + 0` = 3), assignment (`my $v = f()` = 3 â box-set counts), boolean (`f() ? ...`), `scalar(f())`, `defined`, `==`, list context, and the explicit-`return` spelling before #994 (p-return-value's `(not *wantarray*)` + `adjustable-array-p` arm converted it at the RETURN).  So the divergence is exactly the STRING coercion of a raw adjustable vector: `%to-string` / `p-.` / `p-str-eq` / `lc` / `length` treat it as a reference.

WHY IT SURVIVED.  The two spellings disagreed and the disagreement hid it: `sub f { @a }` (implicit tail) handed the live vector out and diverged, while `sub f { return @a }` was converted to a count by `p-return-value` and agreed.  #994 makes the two spellings agree by construction â `p-tail-value` keeps `p-return-value`'s arrayâcount arm, so `return @a` still answers 3 â but the IMPLICIT tail (and every other raw array reaching string context, including the no-sub `@a . ""` case above) is still wrong.

THE FIX, and where it does NOT belong.  It is a coercion-table question: `docs/ir-spec.md` Â§2's to-string rule for a raw adjustable vector.  Do NOT fix it in `%p-leavesub` (the frame exit) â that reads `*wantarray*`, and the `insensitive-call` Kind-A gate deliberately omits the context bind for subs whose returns are provably scalar-rooted, so a value rule keyed on `*wantarray*` there would be right only by accident; and it would leave the no-sub `@a . ""` case untouched anyway.  The one place is the string coercion: an adjustable vector (fill pointer + adjustable = an ARRAY, as opposed to the emitter's simple-vector LIST TEMP, whose scalar answer is its LAST element â `p-list-scalar`) stringifies as its LENGTH.

BAR when it is taken: probe the ten shapes in scratch/arrstr.pl on both emission paths, the full sweep (a coercion change is invisible to corpus-diff), and the op/ companion leg (the s421 rule: a `cl/` coercion/stringification change runs op/).
subject: SILENT WRONG (pre-existing): a raw ARRAY in STRING context stringifies as ARRAY(0x1) instead of its element COUNT -- `@a . ""` is 3 in perl, and lc/length/eq all follow the wrong answer
